text:
harper.design: Observations from today's hallway test: when a run contains 3+ tool calls the current validation blocks are overwhelming. People want a quick scan to know which call failed.

lucas.devex: I was thinking a compact inline status badge next to the tool name. Click expands a small transient panel with a tiny diff excerpt and an "Open inspector" action.

maria.product: That sounds good. We should limit badge text to one word status + optional short reason, e.g. 'Mismatch: price'. Make sure the badge doesn't push content down.

jo.a11y: Accessibility must be first-class: badge needs an accessible name such as "Schema validation for PaymentV2: mismatch" and be operable via keyboard. Popover should use role=dialog and focus management. Also add aria-live announcements when a validation result appears after run completion.

diego.runtime: Backend can provide a cheap validation_summary per invocation to populate the badge and a schema_fingerprint to avoid sending full schema every time. We can also include a tiny JSON snippet as a string: '{"missing": ["price"], "extra": []}' for the popover preview. Full diffs computed async on demand.

lucas.devex: UX details: badge = [SchemaName] [icon] [short text]. Enter/Space opens popover. Popover shows monospace one-line expected vs actual and a link to the right inspector. Support keyboard arrows to jump between multiple badges in a run.

harper.design: Copy suggestions: badge tooltip "Schema: PaymentV2  Mismatch" (note: don't use the word "raw" anywhere). Popover footer: "Open full schema inspector" rather than "View raw JSON".

jo.a11y: Don't rely on color alone for status; include text and an icon. Make sure the badge has aria-expanded and aria-controls. Also include a visible hint in the popover footer about keyboard controls.

deploy-bot: Deploy note: playground-run-detail change queued. Visual test job created: vt-20260323-9.

maria.product: Next steps: diego will add validation_summary and schema_fingerprint to the API, harper will mock badge/popover in Figma, jo will review a11y labels, lucas will prototype client behavior. We'll reconvene when Figma link is up. :sparkles:
